about: The films shown on this public showcase (inventory of 10 Nov 2026; trimmed to 8 films the same day; Defence Factory added later that day). Other releases in this repository may be published but not shown. Durations, sizes and resolutions were measured with ffprobe from the release asset. Dates are when the film was first delivered. Rival films are named by lane or entry (A, B, C), without model or vendor names (POLICY). Films not yet approved for publication are listed in the private video-factory, not here.

families.blurb: Agents prepare, people decide, the proof stays: security work done the agentic way on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

families.name: AWS Factory
families.blurb: The AMI factory: one hardened base image, three workload families, proof in DEV before PROD.

videos.title: Defence Factory — Agents Prepare, People Decide
videos.summary: A 2:09 vision film in the toy world: a team drops in a security warning, agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore find every affected server and prepare one reviewed patch, a person approves once, and the proof goes to audit.

videos.title: Defense Factory — Advisory, Fix, Proof
videos.summary: A 1:11 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: drop a security advisory, see the affected servers (one set aside for a person, one package not ours), approve once, watch the fix run and every server checked again, then open the proof page.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: Defense Factory — It Remembers, It Never Guesses
videos.summary: A 1:03 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: the same warning arrives again and the page says it was handled before (the kernel item still waits for a person), opens the earlier proof, names the file it could not read, refuses to call an empty file an all-clear, and logs every drop in the Audit tab.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: Defense Factory — Mail In, Fix Out
videos.summary: A 0:51 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: a mail file with a table attached is dropped as it is, the page reads the table inside and names the logo it did not read, one approval fixes seven servers, and the proof names the mail and its table. A text-only mail and a scanned PDF are refused honestly on sample data; the lab version reads those.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: Defense Factory — Weekly Patching
videos.summary: A 1:00 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: the Operations tab shows which servers miss patches, a scan only reports, one approval covers the exact list with the restart switch off, the page shows every approved patch installed and six that wait for a restart, and the proof page and the audit log keep who approved what. Sample data: nothing is installed anywhere.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: Defense Factory — Images and Costs
videos.summary: A 1:09 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: after the weekly patching one click makes this month's fully patched server image, one approval replaces the servers one at a time, one click rolls them back, a cost check lists what costs money for nothing and changes nothing, one approval deletes only this project's own leftovers while the rest goes on a list for its owner, and the proof page keeps who approved. Sample data: nothing is made or deleted anywhere.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: Defense Factory — Rules and Earned Trust
videos.summary: A 1:10 demo of the real Defense Factory page on sample data: a rule check reads the account and changes nothing, safe fixes are ticked while a costly fix is not and a person looks where there is no fixed command, one approval runs the fixes and the proof page shows each rule before and after, then a fix type with a clean record is promoted by the Manager with limits, and the L1 ops engineer stops it with one click. Sample data: nothing is read or fixed anywhere.
videos.notes: AI narration. Sample data: invented servers, nothing real runs.

videos.title: AWS Factory — One Image, the Whole Loop
videos.summary: A 1:48 introduction to AWS Factory in the toy world: build only when something changed, prove on real test servers, rehearse the swap, approve, and feed findings back.

videos.title: Nextflow — From Reads to Answers
videos.summary: What Nextflow, nf-core and Sarek do, in plain words: one sequencing run becomes hundreds of millions of reads, and a recipe of steps on little workshop islands turns them into a short list of variants and a quality report.
videos.notes: Plain-words explainer series for everyone. AI narration. Music: "Inspired" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

videos.title: Nextflow Offline — The Sealed Room
videos.summary: Why hospitals, national health data platforms and secure research centres run analyses with no internet, the four things a normal run reaches for online, and the simple recipe to collect, carry and run inside.
videos.notes: Plain-words explainer series for everyone. AI narration. Music: "Inspired" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

videos.title: Nextflow Offline — Prepare Once, Promote Everywhere
videos.summary: The machine we built: a release prepared once in development is copied, never rebuilt, to many sealed research accounts, run once more offline at each destination, and shown to researchers in CloudOS.
videos.notes: Plain-words explainer series for everyone. AI narration. Music: "Inspired" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

videos.title: Nextflow Offline — Prepare Once, Run with Confidence
videos.summary: One real nf-core Sarek test follows the whole journey: hosted and scanned in GitLab, prepared and verified in AWS, run on a sealed island with no internet, and proven with a PASS or FAIL report.
videos.notes: Rebuilt as three islands (mainland, vault, sealed island) with a failure drill. AI narration. Music: "Inspired" by Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com), CC BY 4.0.

videos.title: Nextflow Offline — Prepare Once, Run with Confidence
videos.summary: The first cut of the Nextflow Offline story in the cinematic night look: one missing piece stops an offline run, so everything is prepared, verified and run without a network.

videos.title: Agentic Pentest — What It Can Become
videos.summary: From a lab proof (480 alerts became 69 groups, and the AI has no tools) to a platform vision: every app tested every night by agents, checked by guardrails, judged by experts.
videos.notes: Revision 1 of this vision film was not released.

videos.title: Agentic Pentest POC — From Scanner Noise to Reviewable Findings
videos.summary: Six of 480 recorded scanner alerts travel through a tool-less model that may only propose, a five-check policy gate, and rule-based grouping into one evidence-preserving finding.

videos.title: Patching Running Servers in AWS Factory — Scanned Is Not Patched
videos.summary: How AWS Factory keeps running servers patched with Systems Manager Patch Manager: two roads, three families, the rules, and the trap of scanned-but-not-patched.

videos.title: CIS Hardening in AWS Factory — Fix What We Can, Accept What We Must
videos.summary: 243 CIS checks sort themselves into three buckets: hardened upstream, fixed by us, and accepted risk with owner approval in code, all ending at the release gate.

videos.title: Round 3 — BlueOps: the AMI Factory
videos.summary: An illustrative journey from a golden Amazon Linux 2023 image through a hardened base and three production families to DEV proof and a human-approved rollout.
